fact: Prior knowledge about sensory relationships is important for choosing appropriate actions, but this knowledge can be updated through experience.
source_span: When interacting with the world around us , we largely depend on prior knowledge about the structure of the world and the relationships between the sensory signals resulting from it in order to choose the appropriate action to achieve our goal . This prior knowledge is not necessarily fixed . Rather , through experience we can learn new perceptual [1–3] and sensorimotor relationships ( for reviews see e . g . [4–6] ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on the importance and plasticity of sensorimotor learning.

source_span: For instance , when wearing magnifying glasses , the way in which visual positions relate to actual positions in the real world will change ... we easily adapt our behaviour to this changed relationship in a relatively short amount of time ... selection_reasoning: This fact illustrates the general phenomenon of visuomotor adaptation motivating the study.

selection_reasoning: This fact explains the role of contextual cues in visuomotor learning, relevant to the study's focus on cue-mapping associations.

fact: Previous studies on contextual cue-based visuomotor learning mostly involved only two discrete cue states, limiting understanding of generalisation to novel conditions.
source_span: It is important to note , however , that in most of these studies the role of the learned associations was investigated for only two discrete association-stimulus/visuomotor-mapping pairings . That is , in many of these studies , the context cue could often only have one of two discrete states: the presence or absence of the cue . In this case , testing conditions cannot go beyond the specifically trained pairings to see how the trained pairings generalise to novel conditions ( a cue cannot be half present ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the current study's use of continuous cues to investigate generalisation.

fact: Many contextual cues, like target location, vary continuously, raising questions about how learning generalises and how the number of training pairs affects learning rate.

selection_reasoning: This fact frames the main research question about learning and generalisation with continuous cues.

fact: Applying a simple linear generalisation rule might be faster but may not capture complex nonlinearities in visuomotor mappings, which could slow learning if many samples are needed.
source_span: One could imagine that learning such a rule might in principle be faster than learning the mapping for each and every location separately . However , the structure of a new relationship that needs to be learned can in principle be quite complex . For instance , around the edges of the magnifying glasses large non-linearities in the structure arise . In this respect , applying a general linear rule would not always be beneficial and it might even be better not to generalise beyond the trained conditions at all . To learn the full complexity of the structure we would then have to experience many samples along the full scale of possibilities , which would slow down the learning process .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the trade-offs in generalisation strategies, relevant to interpreting the study's findings.

fact: Generalisation in visuomotor tasks can vary depending on the cues used, with limited generalisation found when training involves only one visual location or discrete task-relevant cues like hand used or movement type.
source_span: Other studies that used only one visual location to train a new visuomotor mapping found that generalisation was more or less restricted to the trained location with a steady decrease in learning effect the further away the test location was from the trained location [19–21] . Very limited generalisation was also found for different starting positions of the movements [22] , different movement speeds [23] , trained left or right hand [13 , 23] and type of movement , i . e . overhand or underhand throwing [13] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the variability and limitations in generalisation found in previous visuomotor learning studies, motivating the current study.

fact: Pre-existing associations between task-relevant cues and visuomotor behavior can interfere with experimental learning and limit generalisation.
source_span: Using task relevant cues poses a problem in the sense that learned associations between the used cues and visuomotor behaviour will likely pre-exist before training starts , simply through experience in normal life . For instance , to interact with objects we often use our left and right hand independently , and from this experience a separate mapping for each hand could already exist with which generalisation of learning for one hand only would have to compete . Such pre-existing associations would , of course , also naturally interfere with any experimental approach .
selection_reasoning: This explains why previous studies using task-relevant cues may have found limited generalisation, providing rationale for the current study's approach.

fact: The present study investigated learning and generalisation of visuomotor mappings using a task-irrelevant continuous cue, target shape, in a rapid pointing task.
source_span: In the present study we circumvented these problems by investigating how learning and generalisation occurs for associations with a task-irrelevant property of the target in a rapid pointing task . fact: If the ANOVA on residuals shows significant differences between shapes, the hypothesis of linear generalisation can be rejected.
source_span: If the learning and transfer of learning occurs in a linear fashion there should not be any difference in the residuals between the different shapes used in the experiment . Thus , if the ANOVA leads to a significant result the hypothesis for linear generalisation can be rejected .

fact: The Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters model simulated participant responses using the exact trial sequences from the experiment, including catch trials.
source_span: For the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters Model , we simulated the sequence of responses using the trial sequences ( i . e . the order of training shapes ) exactly as they had been used for the individual participants in the experiment ( including catch trials ) .

fact: The best fit for each participant in the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters model was found by fitting the learning rate parameter to minimize the mean squared error between human and model responses.
source_span: The best fit for each participant was obtained by fitting the ratio between σy0 and σprocess that determines the learning rate ( one free parameter per participant ) . The fitting procedure was done by minimising the sum of mean squared errors ( between human and model responses ) across trials using a grid search to find the global minimum .

source_span: For the simulations 100 Kalman Filters were included in the mixture , spanning the available shape-space in its entirety ( from ρ = 0 . 01 , a very spiky shape , to ρ = 1 . 0 for circular shapes ) .

fact: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) affect an estimated 2.7 billion of the world's poorest people, causing significant physical debilitation, lowered economic productivity, and social ostracism.
source_span: Neglected tropical diseases ( NTDs ) are parasitic and bacterial diseases that affect an estimated 2 . 7 billion of the world's poorest people , causing significant physical debilitation , lowered economic productivity , and social ostracism for afflicted individuals [1] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the global burden and importance of NTDs, motivating the study.

fact: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy—lymphatic filariasis (LF), trachoma, schistosomiasis, onchocerciasis, and soil-transmitted helminths (STH)—have been targeted for control or elimination.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy: lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis , onchocerciasis and the three soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) ; have been targeted for control or elimination , but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2] .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the diseases targeted by control programs and frames the study's disease focus.

fact: Resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward control and elimination goals for NTDs.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy... have been targeted for control or elimination, but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2].
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the challenge motivating the development of more efficient mapping methods.

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) of at-risk populations with safe and effective drugs is the core public health strategy to fight the five targeted NTDs.
source_span: At the core of public health efforts to fight the five NTDs mentioned above is a strategy of mass drug administration ( MDA ) of at-risk populations with safe and effective drugs often donated by pharmaceutical companies [5] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides context on the intervention that mapping supports.

fact: Before launching MDA, countries must demonstrate that the disease threshold for public health intervention, as established by WHO, has been surpassed.
source_span: Before an MDA can be launched , a country must demonstrate that the disease threshold for public health intervention , as established by the World Health Organization ( WHO ) , has been surpassed [6] , [7] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains why mapping to determine intervention thresholds is necessary.

fact: Currently, each NTD program uses its own mapping methodology, which can be costly and burdensome when multiple surveys are needed in the same country.
source_span: Currently , each NTD program has its own methodology [8] . Conducting multiple surveys in the same country can be costly and burdensome to national disease programs .
selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the need for an integrated mapping approach.

fact: Because NTDs tend to overlap geographically, an integrated mapping approach could result in significant resource savings and more efficient identification of populations needing treatment.
source_span: Because NTDs tend to overlap in geographic areas , it is logical that an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment [9] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides the rationale for developing an integrated mapping protocol.

fact: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) Methodology for lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the main methodological innovation of the study.

fact: The ITM protocol is designed to be resource-efficient and aims to determine whether a disease has reached the threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit.
source_span: The protocol is designed to be resource-efficient , and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the purpose and design goals of the ITM protocol.

fact: The ITM protocol relies on WHO-recommended indicators in disease-specific age groups and uses the district as the sampling frame, except for schistosomiasis where the sub-district is used.
source_span: The protocol relies on World Health Organization ( WHO ) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups . For each disease , the sampling frame was the district , but for schistosomiasis , the sub-district rather than the ecological zone was used .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes key methodological features relevant to understanding the ITM approach.

fact: The ITM methodology was field-tested by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies in one district each in Mali and Senegal.
source_span: We tested the protocol by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies for each of the targeted diseases in one district each in Mali and Senegal .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the study design used to evaluate the ITM protocol.

fact: The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: In this study , the ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma , LF and STH ...
selection_reasoning: This fact reports a principal finding validating the ITM approach for three diseases.

fact: The ITM methodology resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis compared to the WHO methodologies.
source_span: In this study , the ITM methodology ... resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key difference and potential advantage of the ITM method for schistosomiasis.

fact: The ITM methodology was practical, feasible, and demonstrated overall cost savings compared with the standard, non-integrated WHO methodologies.
source_span: ITM was practical , feasible and demonstrated an overall cost saving compared with the standard , non-integrated , WHO methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the significance of the ITM protocol for resource-limited settings.

fact: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed NTD programs in endemic countries.
source_span: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed programs in endemic countries .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the potential public health impact and significance of the ITM methodology.

fact: Trachoma was assessed by examining children aged 1–9 years for active trachoma and females aged 15 years or older for trichiasis using the WHO Simplified Grading System.
source_span: For trachoma , an ophthalmic technician examined both eyes of children aged 1–9 years for clinical signs of active trachoma ( trachomatous inflammation follicular [TF] ) and of females aged ≥15 years for clinical signs of trichiasis ( trachomatous trichiasis [TT] ) using a binocular loupe and natural light according to the WHO Simplified Grading System [12] .
selection_reasoning: This describes the disease context and diagnostic approach for trachoma, a core background and method relevant to the study.

fact: Schistosoma haematobium infection in children aged 6–9 years was detected by testing for haematuria in urine samples using reagent strips.
source_span: For Schistosoma haematobium , the presence of haematuria in urine samples from children aged 6–9 years was detected by urine reagent strips .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides key information on how schistosomiasis was diagnosed, relevant to understanding the study methods and disease focus.

fact: The prevalence and egg load of Schistosoma mansoni and soil-transmitted helminths (STH) were measured using the Kato-Katz method.
source_span: For Schistosoma mansoni and STH , the prevalence and egg load ( eggs per gram of feces ) were calculated using the Kato-Katz method [14] .
selection_reasoning: This describes a principal diagnostic method for key parasitic infections studied, important for understanding the study approach.

fact: Children with active trachoma were treated with tetracycline ointment applied twice daily for six weeks.
source_span: Children who were found to have active trachoma received two tubes of tetracycline ointment , to be applied twice daily for a period of six weeks .
selection_reasoning: This fact relates to the clinical management and intervention following diagnosis, relevant for translational significance.

fact: Females with trichiasis were referred to health centers for trichiasis surgery.
source_span: Females found to have trichiasis were referred to the nearest health center that provides trichiasis surgery .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the clinical follow-up and treatment pathway for a key trachoma complication, important for public health relevance.

fact: Persons testing positive for Wuchereria bancrofti antigen and children infected with Schistosoma haematobium, Schistosoma mansoni, or soil-transmitted helminths were referred to district health centers if mass drug administration (MDA) was not planned.
source_span: Persons who tested positive for W . bancrofti antigen and children who were found to be infected with S . haematobium , S . mansoni or STH were referred to the district health center in case an MDA was not planned in the district .
selection_reasoning: This fact connects diagnostic findings to public health interventions, showing clinical and programmatic relevance.

fact: The study compared two methodologies, the ITM and WHO methods, for mapping neglected tropical diseases including trachoma, schistosomiasis, soil-transmitted helminths, and lymphatic filariasis.
source_span: Results for trachoma , STH and LF were analyzed at the district level for both methodologies ... The public health interventions based on the WHO thresholds ... were compared for both methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the main study question and approach, which is central to the article's purpose.

fact: In Banamba District, Mali, both ITM and WHO methodologies indicated no need for mass drug administration (MDA) for trachoma or soil-transmitted helminths, but both indicated a need for trichiasis surgeries.
source_span: As shown in Figure 3 , the results of both methodologies indicated no need for MDA for trachoma ( ITM Method: 1 . 9% , WHO method: 4 . 7% ... or STH: 0% , 0% ) within the surveyed district . The methodologies were also concordant in indicating a need for TT surgeries ( ITM Method: 2 . 6% , WHO Method: 3 . 7% ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports principal findings comparing the two methods for key diseases, relevant to the study's main results.

fact: The ITM and WHO methodologies differed in their indication for schistosomiasis treatment in Banamba District, with the ITM method identifying more sub-districts needing mass drug administration for the whole population.
source_span: Because the ITM method had as its purpose to refine the schistosomiasis mapping , the two methods differed , in indicating a need for schistosomiasis treatment: the WHO methodology indicated a need for MDA for schistosomiasis among only school-aged children in the entire area . The ITM methodology indicated that four sub-districts were in need of MDA for schistosomiasis among school-aged children only , and that five sub-districts were in need of MDA for schistosomiasis for the whole population .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key difference in mapping outcomes between methodologies, central to the study's conclusions.

fact: Treating the whole population in sub-districts identified by the ITM method for schistosomiasis would result in nearly 33,500 additional at-risk persons being treated compared to treating only school-aged children as indicated by the WHO method.
source_span: Treating the whole population in the sub-districts where this was indicated by the integrated mapping protocol would result in nearly 33 , 500 additional at-risk persons being treated than if only school-aged children in these sub-districts were treated ( as indicated by the WHO protocol ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact quantifies the public health impact of methodological differences, important for significance.

fact: In Diourbel District, Senegal, both ITM and WHO methodologies indicated the need for mass drug administration for trachoma but no need for intervention for soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: Both methodologies indicated the need for MDA for trachoma in the surveyed district ( ITM Method: 14 . 9% , WHO Method: 13 . 4% ) and both methodologies indicated that there was no need for intervention for STH: 0% , 0% .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports key comparative findings in a second study site, supporting the generalizability of results.

fact: Both ITM and WHO methodologies were concordant regarding the need for trichiasis surgeries in Diourbel District, Senegal.
source_span: Both ITM and WHO methodologies were also concordant regarding the need for TT surgeries ( ITM Method: 4 . 7% , WHO Method: 6 . 1% ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact confirms agreement between methods on a key clinical intervention, relevant to study conclusions.

fact: The lymphatic filariasis (LF) mapping was included to validate the feasibility of the integrated mapping approach but not to validate the disease prevalence results.
source_span: The LF mapping was added to validate the feasibility of the integrated mapping and not to validate the results .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the role of LF mapping in the study design, important for understanding study scope.

fact: The Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology is an operational tool designed for Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold for launching disease-specific public health interventions has been reached.
source_span: We describe an integrated NTD mapping methodology ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ) that can be used as an operational tool by Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold needed to launch disease-specific public health intervenions has been reached .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the main purpose and significance of the ITM methodology, which is central to the study.

fact: The ITM methodology balances epidemiologic rigor with field practicality to provide a simpler and quicker way for Ministries of Health to estimate their neglected tropical disease (NTD) needs.
source_span: In developing this ITM methodology , we sought to balance epidemiologic rigour with field practicality , resulting in an approach that can be used only for determining where public health interventions are needed .
selection_reasoning: This explains the motivation and design principle behind the ITM method, important for understanding its value.

fact: The ITM methodology retains key indicators and age groups from WHO disease-specific mapping guidelines but adapts the sampling methodologies for more practical field implementation.
source_span: With the exception of some minor modifications for trachoma , we have retained the key indicators and age groups used in the disease-specific WHO mapping guidelines , but have adapted the sampling methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the methodological approach and how ITM relates to existing WHO protocols.

fact: The ITM methodology reduces costs, manpower, and resource needs compared to the WHO methodology, providing overall cost savings of 31% in Mali and 19% in Senegal.
source_span: The results of the cost data analysis Table 4 , indicate that using the ITM methodology resulted in a 31% overall cost savings in Mali ( $6 , 968 vs . $10 , 039 ) , and a 19% overall cost savings in Senegal ( $8 , 442 vs . $10 , 372 ) .
selection_reasoning: Cost savings and resource efficiency are key findings relevant to the significance and feasibility of the ITM approach.

fact: The ITM methodology used resources more efficiently than the WHO methodology in travel, supplies, and team training in both Mali and Senegal.
source_span: In both countries , the ITM methodology used resources more efficiently than the WHO methodology in the areas of travel , supplies and team training , as shown in Table 4 .
selection_reasoning: This supports the claim of improved efficiency and feasibility of the ITM method.

fact: In Mali, the ITM methodology identified more sub-districts needing mass drug administration (MDA) for schistosomiasis, including some for whole population treatment, compared to the WHO methodology which recommended MDA only for school-aged children.
source_span: The WHO methodology indicated a need for MDA for schistosomiasis treatment among only school-aged children in the entire area , while the ITM methodology indicated six sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis among school-aged children only , four sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis for the whole population and one sub-district which did not pass the threshold for treatment .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key difference in public health intervention decisions resulting from the ITM versus WHO methods.

fact: Compared to the district-based WHO protocol, the ITM methodology targeted nearly 46,000 extra at-risk individuals for schistosomiasis treatment in Mali.
source_span: Compared to the district based WHO protocol , the ITM methodology targeted nearly 46 , 000 extra at-risk individuals for treatment .
selection_reasoning: This quantifies the increased reach of the ITM method, important for understanding its public health impact.

fact: The ITM methodology uses program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO, with minor adaptations for trachoma, to allow use of WHO thresholds and reduce the number of people undergoing multiple tests.
source_span: In our ITM mapping protocol , we insisted on using the program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO with the exception of some adaptation for trachoma . The advantage of using these established age groups was that the WHO thresholds were applicable and that few people had to undergo multiple tests and examinations; only in a limited number of cases were people asked to undergo more than one test or examination .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies how the ITM method maintains compatibility with WHO standards while improving field practicality.

fact: The ITM protocol uses a convenience sample in each village to facilitate data collection and improve time efficiency compared to house-to-house visits used in the WHO trachoma protocol.
source_span: In each village , we chose to use a convenience sample for reasons of field practicality . Asking people of different ages to come to a central location in each village facilitated data collection and was much more time-efficient than house-to-house visits , such as those used in the WHO trachoma protocol .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key methodological adaptation that improves feasibility and speed of data collection.

fact: The ITM and WHO methodologies resulted in the same public health recommendations in the field testing conducted in Mali and Senegal.
source_span: As the field testing in both countries showed , the data of both methodologies resulted in the same public health recommendations .
selection_reasoning: This supports the validity of the ITM method in guiding intervention decisions.

fact: The ITM methodology is not designed to provide epidemiologically correct prevalence data or to serve as a baseline for measuring impact at the district level.
source_span: To understand the value and limitations of this protocol , it is critical to understand that this protocol is not claiming to provide epidemiologically correct prevalence data because both the villages and the individuals tested were not randomly selected . First , this implies that we cannot recommend using findings from this methodology as a baseline for measuring impact at the district level .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the intended use and limitations of the ITM method, important for accurate interpretation.

fact: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for lymphatic filariasis, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths but uses a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation.
source_span: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for LF , schistosomiasis and STH , but we used a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the study's methodological innovation while preserving standard disease metrics, which is central to the research question and approach.

fact: To improve representativeness for the trachomatous inflammation—follicular (TF) indicator, the study selected a predetermined number of children aged 1–5 and 6–9 to prevent biased prevalence estimates.
source_span: To improve the representativeness for the TF indicator , we selected a pre-determined number of children between the ages of 1–5 and 6–9 . This was intended to prevent biased estimates in case the 6–9 year age group made up the majority of children being graded for trachoma because prevalence rates are highest in 1–5 year olds .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key sampling strategy to ensure accurate disease prevalence estimates, relevant to the study's methodology and findings.

fact: The study used women above the age of 15 years to measure trachomatous trichiasis (TT) prevalence, based on expert consultation and literature review.
source_span: After consultation with trachoma experts , we decided to use women above the age of 15 yrs [22] .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies a key decision in defining the adult population for TT measurement, important for interpreting prevalence results.

fact: The ITM methodology links the sampling frame directly to the implementation unit for mass drug administration (MDA) for each neglected tropical disease to improve public health action feasibility.
source_span: Because the ITM methodology is focused on public health action , the sampling frame is directly linked to the implementation unit for MDA for each of the NTDs .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the practical significance of the methodology for guiding interventions, a core study motivation and implication.

fact: The study used the district as the primary implementation unit for soil-transmitted helminths (STH) because a village-centered approach is difficult for large-scale national program implementation and supervision.
source_span: Because a village-centered approach is difficult for implementation and supervision for a large-scale national program , we decided to use the district as the primary implementation unit for STH as it is recommended by WHO for LF and trachoma .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key methodological choice affecting intervention planning, relevant to the study's design and findings.

fact: Both the ITM and WHO methodologies concluded that no intervention was necessary for soil-transmitted helminths in the two countries studied, confirming the reliability of the ITM methodology.
source_span: Our methodology found the same public health intervention for trachoma and for STH . For STH , both methodologies concluded that no intervention was necessary , which confirmed the reliability of our methodology in the two countries .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports a principal finding validating the new methodology against the WHO standard.

fact: For schistosomiasis, the study recommends using the sub-district as the implementation unit to better target treatment because the disease is very focal and treatment medication is costly and limited.
source_span: In the case of schistosomiasis , a disease that is very focal in nature , and for which treatment medication is costly and in limited supply , we feel that it would be more appropriate to use the sub-district as implementation units to determine needs for treatment because a district-based approach may result in overtreating or undertreating subpopulations within the district [23] .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses a key finding and recommendation for improving treatment targeting and resource use.

fact: Using the sub-district as the implementation unit for schistosomiasis allowed the identification of highly endemic and low endemic sub-areas within districts that were not identified using the WHO-recommended ecological zone.
source_span: Our results show that by using the sub-district as I . U . , the MDA will be more targeted to people at risk . In our study , when the WHO-recommended ecological zone was used as the implementation unit , highly endemic ( prevalence of >50% ) or low endemic ( prevalence of <10% ) sub-areas of the district were not identified , but were identified by the integrated methodology .
selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates a principal finding that the integrated methodology improves disease mapping precision.

fact: Using the WHO protocol for schistosomiasis mapping would have resulted in undertreating tens of thousands of people in highly endemic areas and overtreating others not in need of treatment, as shown in Senegal.
source_span: As a result , using the WHO protocol would have meant that tens of thousands of people living in highly endemic areas would not have received treatment , and that other people not in need of treatment would have been treated , as would have been the case in Senegal .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the public health significance of the improved mapping approach.

fact: The integrated mapping approach was more efficient in cost, transport, time in the field, and use of human resources compared to the WHO methodologies.
source_span: The integrated approach proved to be more efficient in cost , transport , time in the field and the use of human resources .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a key advantage of the integrated methodology relevant to implementation and policy.

fact: The integrated mapping team used one vehicle and five experienced technicians performing multiple tasks, compared to the WHO methodologies which used three vehicles and seven-member teams.
source_span: The ITM methodology used one vehicle to transport the team , versus 3 used in the WHO methodologies , employed a 5-member team instead of a 7-member team , and took about half as much time to implement as the WHO methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides concrete evidence of resource efficiency supporting the integrated approach.

fact: Cost savings from integrated mapping include reduced planning and logistic preparations, which is valuable for overburdened health staff.
source_span: It is also important to mention that certain cost savings from integrated mapping such as time saved by only having to plan one survey compared with several different protocol meetings and logistic preparations is priceless for overburdened health staff .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains an important practical benefit of integration beyond direct financial costs.

fact: Mapping is often the first field activity of an integrated neglected tropical disease program, and the integrated mapping team demonstrated the concept of integrating vertical programs at all levels of the Ministry of Health.
source_span: mapping is often the first field activity of an integrated NTD program , and the creation of the team demonstrated the concept of integrating vertical programs to all levels of the MoH and this first activity can help with further collaboration for implementing integrated public health interventions .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the broader significance of the integrated mapping approach for health system integration.

fact: Although the ITM methodology resulted in substantial cost savings compared to the WHO methodology, the cost depends on the number of sub-units in a district, which can increase sampling size for schistosomiasis.
source_span: Although the ITM methodology resulted in substantial cost savings compared to the WHO methodology , the cost depends on the number of sub-units in a district . This means , for example , that the sampling size for schistosomiasis could be much higher using the ITM methodology than using the WHO methodology .
selection_reasoning: This fact qualifies the cost advantage by noting a trade-off related to sampling intensity.

fact: A more targeted mass drug administration for schistosomiasis is important because donated praziquantel is limited in availability.
source_span: However , this would result in a more targeted MDA for schistosomiasis , which is important because there is limited availability of donated praziquantel .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the clinical and resource rationale for targeted treatment.

fact: Health workers are not always well-informed about where schistosomiasis is most prevalent, as indicated by results from both the ITM and WHO methodologies.
source_span: The results from both the ITM and WHO methologies indicate that health workers are not always well-informed about where schistosomiasis is most prevalent .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies a knowledge gap motivating improved mapping.

fact: Treatment decisions based on purposely-selected villages did not systematically result in more treatments than those based on randomly-selected villages.
source_span: The results show that treatment decisions , based on the purposely-selected villages , did not systematically result in more treatments than those based on the randomly-selected villages .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses a key comparison relevant to sampling strategy and treatment planning.

fact: This study presents a novel integrated mapping protocol to determine whether thresholds for public health interventions for neglected tropical diseases have been reached.
source_span: This study shows a novel integrated mapping protocol to determine whether thresholds for public health interventions have been reached.
selection_reasoning: Introducing the new mapping protocol is central to the study's main contribution and aligns with the abstract-level claim about the method.

fact: The integrated mapping approach is logistically practical, cost-efficient, and flexible.
source_span: The approach is logistically practical , cost-efficient and flexible .
selection_reasoning: The practical advantages of the new approach are key findings relevant for its potential adoption and public health impact.

fact: For schistosomiasis, the integrated mapping approach results in more targeted mass drug administrations compared with the district-level implementation currently used by most integrated neglected tropical disease programs.
source_span: For schistosomiasis , our approach also results in more targeted MDAs compared with the district level implementation currently adapted by most integrated NTD program .
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights a specific benefit of the new protocol for schistosomiasis control, important for translational relevance.

fact: The protocol uses mainly age-specific disease indicators as recommended by the World Health Organization.
source_span: The protocol uses mainly the age-specific disease indicators as recommended by WHO .
selection_reasoning: Describing the key measurement approach connects the method to WHO standards, important background for understanding the study.

fact: The integrated mapping protocol sets the stage for subsequent integrated program activities essential for neglected tropical disease elimination and control.
source_span: Further , it sets the stage for all of the following integrated program activities essential for NTD elimination and control .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the significance and potential impact of the protocol beyond initial mapping.

fact: The study identified a limitation that nine of the 60 trachoma villages sampled were selected for both mapping methodologies, which may have introduced selection bias.
source_span: The main limitation for the trachoma mapping is that a total of nine of the 60 trachoma villages sampled were selected for both methodologies .
selection_reasoning: Acknowledging limitations is important for balanced interpretation and aligns with abstract-level discussion of study constraints.

fact: In six of the nine villages sampled by both methods, up to 62% of the sample was selected by convenience, likely introducing selection bias.
source_span: for the other six villages , a selection bias was likely introduced because up to 62% of the sample was selected by convenience only and those persons would maybe not have been included if the sample was collected randomly .

fact: To reduce the burden on inhabitants, the study included data collected in the integrated mapping for the WHO method and added only 30 children by visiting households.
source_span: To decrease the burden of the inhabitants by not having the same children examined twice , we included the data collected in the integrated mapping for the WHO method and added only 30 children by visiting the households .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key methodological decision relevant to the study design and data collection.

fact: Based on lessons learned and feedback, the integrated mapping approach requires modifications to ensure the most useful data are collected.
source_span: Based on the lessons learned from the implementation in the first two countries and feedback we received form NTD colleagues , we do recognize that this novel mapping approach requires some modification to ensure that the most useful data are collected .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses the ongoing refinement of the method, important for understanding the study's implications.

fact: An adapted integrated mapping protocol with randomly selected villages and other minor changes is currently being field tested.
source_span: For this reason , we are currently field testing an adapted protocol with all villages selected randomly among other minor changes .
selection_reasoning: This fact indicates future directions and improvements, relevant for the study's significance.

fact: Stem cells have an innate ability to occupy their stem cell niche, which is optimized to house stem cells.

The bioluminescence signal was also reduced in LAC::lux ΔclfB infected animals compared to LAC::lux infected mice ( Fig 1C and 1D ) . The reduction in bioluminescence signal was validated by quantifying the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 ( Fig 1E ) and day 6 ( Fig 1F ) .
